title: CERN Node
main_text: EOSC Federation · First wave Node The CERN EOSC Node for Open Science Integrating CERN's world-class research services and FAIR data into the European Open Science Cloud, enabling reproducible workflows, open datasets, and cross-disciplinary collaboration for researchers everywhere. Get Started Explore Services Try an Analysis What is the CERN EOSC Node? Part of the European Open Science Cloud Federation The CERN EOSC Node strengthens the EOSC Federation by providing high-TRL services and technology essential for high-energy physics and interdisciplinary research. It integrates CERN's established platforms such as Rucio, REANA, FTS, CERNBox, Zenodo, and the CERN VRE into a federated European infrastructure. The objective is to support the exploitation of FAIR CERN Open Data through reproducible workflows, analysis facilities, and cross-disciplinary collaboration, making particle physics data and tools accessible to the broader scientific community. “Building a successful federation is not just about the infrastructure but it's about making sure that the users are part of the co-design of the services. This is one of the reasons for the success of the WLCG, a federation of over 170 data centres spanning more than 40 countries.” — [removed], EOSC Association Find Your Path Get started based on what brings you here Researchers Run analyses on open data, manage large datasets, and publish reproducible workflows. Policy Makers Understand what the Node delivers, its maturity, and how to engage with it. Infrastructure Operators Reuse the open-source stack and federate your own infrastructure with the Node. Core Principles What drives open science at CERN Open Data CERN provides curated open data and analyses from its flagship particle physics experiments, preserved with long-term discoverability through the CERN Open Data portal and Zenodo. Interoperable Services CERN services use standard protocols and open APIs to enable interoperability across the EOSC Federation. Federated AAI, shared catalogues, and common data management tools ensure seamless integration with other nodes and research infrastructures. Reusable Workflows Containerised analysis pipelines on REANA or Jupyter can be shared, re-executed, and adapted by anyone. Near-data computation sends workflows to where datasets live, making results verifiable and building on prior work. Services Key services onboarded to the EOSC Federation View the full catalogue CERN Open Data Data Discovery Access collision data, simulated datasets, and educational resources from CERN experiments. CERN VRE Pre-production Interactive Analysis Powered by SWAN (Service for Web based ANalysis) — a platform to perform interactive data analysis in the cloud using Jupyter notebooks. CERNBox Storage Cloud sync and share service allowing users to store and share data seamlessly across all their devices. REANA Pre-production Analysis Workflows Reusable Analysis platform. Allows researchers to run containerised data analysis pipelines on distributed compute clouds. Rucio Data Management Scientific Data Management system providing a complete and scalable solution for managing large volumes of data across globally distributed centres. Zenodo Beta Publishing General-purpose open repository enabling researchers to deposit educational materials, datasets, software, and publications. View the full catalogue Virtual Research Environment The CERN VRE for cross-disciplinary science The CERN Virtual Research Environment is a modular, scalable platform that integrates software provisioning (CVMFS), data management (Rucio), reproducible workflows (REANA), and interactive analysis (Jupyter) into a unified workspace. Unlike a generic cloud notebook (Google Colab, AWS SageMaker, Azure ML), the VRE ships pre-configured with the specialised toolchains scientific communities actually need: HEP software stacks via CVMFS, federated AAI, direct access to experiment data lakes, and analysis pipelines that run close to the data rather than shuttling petabytes across the public internet. Access the VRE Browse Analyses Node Status See the rollout stages → View the status page → Current deployment phase of the CERN Node Phase 1 — Build-up Completed Onboarded CERN technology into the EOSC EU Node and tested the virtual credit model. Services including REANA, VRE, Zenodo, CERN Open Data, HEPData, and INSPIRE-HEP were successfully integrated. March – December 2025 Phase 2 — Production Active Establishing the CERN Node with quotas and controlled resource allocation, full federated AAI, and helpdesk support. Started Q1 2026 Open Science at CERN Training, outreach, and community At CERN, the practice of open science is key to delivering on the organisational mission. CERN Open Science encompasses an evolving ecosystem of policies, initiatives, services, and technologies, driven by people from across the organisation with the goal to maximise the global impact of research. Open Access Open Data Open Source Open Hardware Citizen Science Learn more at openscience.cern Competence Centre & Training Learn to leverage HEP software frameworks, Machine Learning tools, and distributed infrastructure through curated training programs. Data Management Plans Guidelines and templates for managing research data throughout the project lifecycle, aligned with FAIR principles. Contributing Organisations CERN departments, INSPIRE-HEP collaboration (DESY, Fermilab, IHEP, IN2P3, SLAC), Durham University, and ESCAPE partners.

children.main_text: Contact The Node offers two support channels. Each channel suits a different kind of request. EOSC Federation Forum Use the Forum for a question with a lasting answer, such as how something works or why an error occurs. Other users can find the answer later. Browse the CERN Node category Ask a new question CERN Node Helpdesk Open a helpdesk ticket for an incident, an outage, or an access request. Use it also for any task that needs an owner and a deadline. The team tracks the ticket until it closes. eosc-service-desk@cern.ch Not sure which channel to use? Start with the Forum. The team opens a ticket for you if the request needs one. For questions about the EOSC Federation more broadly, see the EOSC Association .

children.title: CERN Node
children.main_text: The CERN Node A first-wave node of the EOSC Federation The CERN Node strengthens the EOSC Federation by providing high-TRL services and technology essential for high-energy physics and interdisciplinary research. It integrates CERN's established platforms, including Rucio, REANA, CERNBox, Zenodo, and the CERN Virtual Research Environment, into a federated European infrastructure. The objective is to support the exploitation of FAIR CERN Open Data through reproducible workflows, analysis facilities, and cross-disciplinary collaboration, making particle physics data and tools accessible to the broader scientific community. Rollout stages Stages describe what the Node offers you. Programme phases, further down this page, describe how we are building it. Stage 1 Available Education and outreach Education & Outreach-Focused Node Schools, universities, teachers and students, and anyone meeting real particle-physics data for the first time. The Node opens with the full CERN Open Data corpus, curated tutorials, and pre-configured analyses that run end to end in the browser with no setup, in the SWAN-powered VRE and as reproducible REANA workflows. This is the default experience for anyone who signs in. ✓ The full CERN Open Data corpus ✓ Curated tutorials ✓ Ready-made analyses that run end to end via the VRE ✓ A session sized for teaching and first analyses Good to know: Sessions are shared and modest: enough for a classroom exercise or a first real analysis, not for a large study. Signing in gets you this default experience, but each underlying tool (e.g. the VRE, REANA, CERNBox) is still requested individually from the services catalogue, not granted automatically. Available since public launch (October 2026) Stage 2 In progress Research on open data Education and Research Node for Open Data Theorists, phenomenologists, and researchers taking a study on CERN open data to research grade. Everything in stage 1, and the Node also supports real research: collaborators bring their own code and run autonomous analysis against the open-data corpus, and package the result as a reproducible REANA workflow of their own. ✓ Autonomous analysis with your own code ✓ Package your own workflows for REANA ✓ Allocations beyond the teaching-sized default where the science needs them Good to know: Capacity is finite and shared, so anything beyond the default is decided case by case rather than granted automatically. The software delivery path for bring-your-own-code is still being designed. At public launch (October 2026) Stage 3 Planned Multi-tier research node Multi-tiered Research Node with Extra Services for CERN Users The open-data community, joined by CERN users working on the LHC and other experiments. A multi-tier, research-capable platform within the EOSC Federation. Here, CERN users get full access to the power and capabilities of the central CERN facility on top of the Node's baseline services, and the scope moves beyond open data: researchers can work directly with their experiments' own data. ✓ Full access to the central CERN facility's compute and storage power ✓ Work with experiment data, not just the open-data corpus ✓ Access for CERN users to the Node's baseline services Good to know: This stage is planned, not scheduled. After launch What to expect The Node is public research infrastructure with finite, shared capacity. It is not a commercial cloud, and it does not try to be: sessions are sized for analysis of open data, and fair-use limits apply. If your work needs more than that, get in touch and we will look at it case by case. For concrete figures, see the FAQ . Coming to this page Documentation and features we plan adding as the Node matures. User / use policy Done Terms governing who can use the Node and how. Published at public launch (October 2026) Flexible, customisable quota limits Planned A more granular resource-allocation model, beyond today's fixed teaching-sized default. After launch (targeted Q1 2027) Architecture description In progress How the Node's services fit together technically. After launch (targeted November 2026) Use cases documentation In progress Worked examples of how different kinds of users put the Node to work. After launch (targeted Q4 2026) Track live service uptime on the status page , browse the full services catalogue , check the FAQ , or see who else is involved on the Scientific Collaboration page. This Node is also listed on the EOSC Federation site ↗ .

children.title: CERN Node
children.main_text: CERN The European Organization for Nuclear Research CERN is one of the world's largest centres for scientific research, straddling the Franco-Swiss border near Geneva. Founded in 1954, it is a collaboration between its Member States that operates the world's largest particle physics laboratory, home to the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) and the experiments that use it, including ATLAS, CMS, ALICE, and LHCb. CERN's scientific programme has produced discoveries that reshape our understanding of the universe, most notably the 2012 observation of the Higgs boson. Beyond physics, CERN has a long history of open collaboration and technology transfer: the World Wide Web itself was created at CERN in 1989 to help physicists share information. Our mission Fundamental Physics Research Perform world-class research to uncover what the universe is made of and how it works, from the Higgs boson to the open questions beyond the Standard Model. Advanced Infrastructure Provide unique particle accelerators and detectors, pushing them to the frontiers of human knowledge in a sustainable and environmentally responsible way. Global Collaboration Unite people from all over the world to push the frontiers of science and technology, for the benefit of all: a model of peaceful, open international cooperation. Education & Engagement Train the scientists and engineers of tomorrow, and share the excitement of fundamental science with everyone. That same culture of openness drives CERN's participation in open science today: curated open datasets from LHC experiments, open-source scientific software used across the research community, and infrastructure built to be shared far beyond particle physics. The CERN Node is one expression of that mission, making CERN's data, tools, and expertise available to the broader European research community through the European Open Science Cloud. Learn more at home.cern

children.title: Policies — CERN Node
children.main_text: ← Home Policies These three documents govern use of the CERN EOSC Node and of every service reached through it. Each service also keeps its own terms, which prevail for that service. Acceptable Use Policy and Conditions of Use The rules you agree to when you use the Node’s services. User Access Policy Who can use the services, and how you get access to them. Terms and Conditions What the Node is, what it does not promise, and whose terms apply. CERN-wide policies CERN Computing Rules (OC5) The general computing rules that apply to all use of CERN's computing facilities. CERN Data Privacy Protection Policy How CERN, as the Node's operator, processes your personal data. CERN EOSC Node Privacy Notice The personal data the Node itself processes, such as sign-in and access requests. Analytics Matomo The Node uses Matomo, hosted by CERN, to count visits and see which pages are useful. Tracking is first-party only: we do not set a cookie, we do not share data with third parties, and do not follow you across other sites. Your IP address is anonymized before it is stored, and your browser is excluded automatically if it sends a "Do Not Track" signal. Opt out of analytics

Learn about the open-source technology behind these services → Service stages and TRL of the integration in the CERN Node The Technology Readiness Level (TRL) describes how mature the service is inside the CERN Node. It does not describe the service itself. No badge Production · TRL 9 actual system proven in operational environment The service is fully operational and supported. Beta Beta · TRL 7 system prototype demonstration in operational environment You can use the service now. Some actions need a sign-in that is not the EOSC AAI. Pre-production Pre-production · TRL 6 technology demonstrated in relevant environment The service is listed but not open yet. You cannot request access. children.title: CERN Node
children.main_text: Scientific Collaboration Open science at CERN, and the community behind the Node Open Science at CERN At CERN, the practice of open science is key to delivering on the organisational mission. CERN Open Science encompasses an evolving ecosystem of policies, initiatives, services, and technologies, driven by people from across the organisation with the goal to maximise the global impact of research, spanning open access, open data, open source, open hardware, and citizen science. The CERN Node extends that practice into the EOSC Federation, in collaboration with partner institutions across high-energy physics and beyond. Competence Centre & Training Learn to leverage HEP software frameworks, Machine Learning tools, and distributed infrastructure through curated training programs. Data Management Plans Guidelines and templates for managing research data throughout the project lifecycle, aligned with FAIR principles. Contributing Organisations CERN departments, INSPIRE-HEP collaboration (DESY, Fermilab, IHEP, IN2P3, SLAC), Durham University, and ESCAPE partners. Learn more at openscience.cern ESCAPE CERN also pursues open science through ESCAPE , the European Science Cluster of Astronomy & Particle Physics ESFRI Research Infrastructures, in which CERN participates alongside partner institutions from astronomy, nuclear, and particle physics, working toward shared, FAIR-compliant services connected to EOSC. The direction of travel in scientific computing, well beyond ESCAPE, is federation. The Worldwide LHC Computing Grid (WLCG) , around 160 computing centres in more than 40 countries built to store, distribute, and analyse the LHC's data, has long shown how a federated model can work at this scale. High-performance computing is moving the same way, and initiatives such as the EOSC Federation pursue a similar goal for the broader Open Science ecosystem: democratising access to computing capabilities, in the spirit of WLCG, with CERN among the participants. ESCAPE sits at the intersection of these federations, co-developing shared infrastructure and tools so that researchers can draw on heterogeneous resources without the overhead of managing each one separately. Looking ahead, the collaboration has set out its Distributed Computing Roadmap for 2026–2030 , coordinating computing infrastructure strategy across particle physics and astronomy partners including CERN, the Einstein Telescope, the Square Kilometer Array Observatory, the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory, and several other communities. Learn more at projectescape.eu

children.title: Acceptable Use Policy — CERN Node
children.main_text: ← Policies Acceptable Use Policy and Conditions of Use Version 1.0 · Intended audience: CERN EOSC Node users This Acceptable Use Policy and Conditions of Use (“AUP”) defines the rules and conditions that govern your access to and use (including transmission, processing, and storage of data) of the resources and services (“Services”) as granted by CERN for the purpose of scientific research in the European Open Science Cloud. You shall only use the Services in a manner consistent with the purposes and limitations of this Acceptable Use Policy; you shall show consideration towards other users including by not causing harm to the Services; you have an obligation to collaborate in the resolution of issues arising from your use of the Services. You shall only use the Services for lawful purposes and not breach, attempt to breach, nor circumvent administrative or security controls. You shall respect intellectual property and confidentiality agreements. You shall protect your access credentials (e.g. passwords, private keys or multi-factor tokens); you shall not share them with any other person or system. You shall keep your registered information correct and up to date. You shall promptly report known or suspected security breaches, credential compromise, or misuse to the security contact stated below; and report any compromised credentials to the relevant issuing authorities. Reliance on the Services shall only be to the extent specified by any applicable service level agreement for that Service; use without such an agreement is at your own risk. Each Service’s own terms of use, linked under Service-specific information , state whether one applies. Your personal data will be processed in accordance with the CERN Data Privacy Protection Policy and the Privacy Notice of the Service you use, linked under Service-specific information . Your use of the Services may be restricted, suspended or withdrawn for administrative, operational, or security reasons, without prior notice and without compensation. If you violate this AUP, you may be liable for the consequences, which may include your account being suspended and a report being made to your home organisation or to law enforcement. You must abide by CERN Computing Rules (OC5), the OC5 Subsidiary Rules, and the CERN Security Principles . Your use of the Services may be logged for operational, accounting, auditing, and security purposes, in accordance with the applicable CERN policies. You may be contacted by the Service operators or the CERN Computer Security Office in relation to operational or security incidents involving your use of the Services, and you shall cooperate with them in the investigation and resolution of such incidents. The Services shall be used for non-military purposes only. Service-specific information Clause 8 refers to the privacy statements the Services follow. children.link_text: User Access Policy Who can use the services, and how you get access to them.
children.title: User Access Policy — CERN Node
children.main_text: ← Policies User Access Policy Version 1.0 · Intended audience: CERN EOSC Node users This User Access Policy (“UAP”) explains who may use the resources and services of the CERN EOSC Node (“Services”), and how you obtain access to them. You sign in with an account from an identity provider that the EOSC Federation recognises. You do not need a CERN account. Signing in proves who you are. It does not by itself give you access to a Service. Some Services are open. You use them anonymously, or immediately after you sign in, with no request needed. The Services catalogue marks which these are. Other Services need an access request. Sign in, open the Services catalogue, and select Request Access on the Service you need. A CERN EOSC Node administrator reviews your request, and you receive the decision by email. Access decisions use your identity and the attributes supplied through the federated AAI, such as your affiliation, your group memberships, your roles, or your Virtual Organisation membership. Each Service operator sets and applies the authorisation rules for that Service, and those rules prevail for that Service. The Node opens in defined rollout stages, and the stage sets the default allocation. Capacity is finite and shared, so anything beyond the default of the current stage is decided case by case rather than granted automatically. The rollout stages state what each stage includes and what it does not. Your access may be restricted, suspended or withdrawn if you no longer meet the authorisation requirements, for administrative, operational, or security reasons, without prior notice and without compensation, or if you do not comply with the Acceptable Use Policy or the applicable CERN policies. If you need help Write to eosc-service-desk@cern.ch . You do not need to sign in to contact the helpdesk. Applicable policies [1] CERN EOSC Node Acceptable Use Policy and Conditions of Use [2] AARC Blueprint Architecture 2025 (AARC-G080)

children.title: CERN Node
children.main_text: Open Source Technology The CERN Node services are built on mature, openly developed software to handle the scale of the LHC. Every project below is open source and links to its upstream repository, so the technology behind the Node is fully transparent and reusable. Rucio Data Management The scientific data management framework behind the Node's data services. Rucio organises, locates, and replicates large volumes of data across globally distributed storage, originally built to manage the exabytes produced by the LHC experiments. Source Code Project Site → REANA Reproducible Workflows The reproducible analysis platform that runs containerised pipelines on distributed compute clouds. REANA captures the full computational workflow (inputs, code, and environment) so results can be re-executed and verified by anyone. Source Code Project Site → SWAN Interactive Analysis The Jupyter-based interactive analysis service powering the CERN VRE. SWAN ships pre-configured scientific software stacks and connects notebooks directly to CERN storage and compute. Source Code Project Site → CVMFS Software Distribution The CernVM File System distributes scientific software stacks worldwide over HTTP. It lets analysis environments load the exact toolchains they need on demand, without local installation, underpinning reproducibility across the Node. Source Code Project Site → CERNBox Sync & Share CERNBox is the CERN Cloud Storage provided to the CERN community. It is powered by Reva, which implements open APIs to connect sync-and-share storage to applications and federated services across research infrastructures. Source Code Project Site → Open Cloud Mesh Federation Open Cloud Mesh (OCM) is a server-to-server protocol designed to enable sharing across independent administrative domains, thus federating storage and compute resources. While its primary use-case is Enterprise File Sync&Share systems, OCM is also being implemented for more general use-cases. Source Code Project Site → File Transfer Service Data Transfer The File Transfer Service (FTS) is responsible for reliably moving the bulk of LHC data between sites. FTS schedules, optimises, and monitors large-scale transfers across the World-wide Computing Grid. Source Code Project Site → Invenio Digital Repositories The open digital-library framework powering Zenodo, the CERN Open Data portal, INSPIRE-HEP, and HEPData. Invenio handles preservation, metadata, DOIs, and discovery for FAIR research outputs. Source Code Project Site → Indico Event Management The event-management platform used worldwide for conferences, meetings, and lectures. Indico is developed at CERN and released as open source for the wider research community. Source Code Project Site →
